prize_parts.citation: for experimental discovery of the distance and medium dependence of long-range electron tunnelling through proteins

statement.case_for: Long-range electron transfer through proteins is a mechanism stated in physical terms and tested quantitatively. Photo-triggered, ruthenium-modified proteins with time-resolved kinetics showed that rates fall off exponentially with distance and depend on the intervening polypeptide, and this became the working framework for electron flow in respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes. The experimental attribution is compact and clean (Gray and Winkler), the work has decades of independent confirmation, and it explains how biology moves charge across large distances. Marcus's 1992 prize covered the theory of electron transfer, not this experimental demonstration in proteins, so a prize here is a distinct achievement and not a repeat.
statement.case_against: This is my own field's neighbourhood, so I discount my enthusiasm. The opening ballots show little support: no colleague ranked it first, and several do not place it in their top five. The 1992 Marcus prize may make some members see it as a continuation of already honoured electron transfer theory. The tunnelling-pathway theory of Beratan and Onuchic sits beside the experiments and is not credited here. The strongest competing candidates (B011 and B068) have broader support and a more obviously single, attributable discovery.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B011) turned aryl amine construction into a general, routine operation through ligand design, with 25 years of confirmation and heavy industrial use. A Buchwald and Hartwig pair is clean, and Kosugi is only a narrower precursor.
responses.response: I agree the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and the maturity is not in doubt, which is why I name B011 as an alternative. My qualification is that the committee should check what Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry already established before we call the achievement entirely original to the two. I would also want the expert reports to show the mechanistic work on the catalytic cycle and not only the synthetic scope, since we are weighing a discovery and not usage statistics. If that holds, I would not oppose B011.

responses.point: Nitrogenase (B003) rests on decisive crystal structures of the FeMo-cofactor, including the interstitial carbide, with Rees and Einsle as the structural anchors and Seefeldt contributing mechanism. Zou notes that the catalytic mechanism is still only partly resolved.
responses.response: I largely share this reading, since I proposed the same three names in my own opening. I take her maturity point seriously: a prize would honour the structure and cofactor framework, while the N2 binding site and the E4 hydride state are still being argued. That makes the citation harder to word safely. Dean and Ribbe also have strong claims, and the three-person limit forces a cut that the genetic and biochemical line may contest. I therefore place B003 below B053 but keep it as a leading alternative.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B068) turns the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a designable chemical tool, with PROTACs from Crews and Deshaies and cereblon-based glues from Handa, and many degraders in clinical trials.
responses.response: The concept is real and the mechanism is well characterised, so I do not dismiss it. I disagree on timing and attribution. No PROTAC is yet approved, and Aili's own text concedes that clinical validation is pending. The field also has many valid claimants (Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito). The credited set separates into at least two distinct strands (PROTAC concept and cereblon glues), which makes a clean three-name citation difficult. I would regard B068 as a strong candidate for a later year and not for this one.

responses.point: Dye-sensitised solar cells (B039) show a clear kinetic principle, with charge separation at a mesoporous interface and Grätzel and O'Regan as the core credit. Linke also raises whether the 1980 Sanger sequencing prize limits a sequencing award (B005).
responses.response: I agree that the interfacial electron-transfer kinetics behind B039 are quantitative and physically well grounded, and the field is mature. I do not agree that Hagfeldt can simply be left out without reading the expert report on who carried the mechanistic understanding. On B005, I share the worry about the sequencing precedent. The chemistry of reversible terminators is plainly distinct from Sanger's, but the committee should settle that question explicitly and not assume it.

responses.point: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (B001) give near-quantum accuracy at force-field cost and have changed what can be simulated, with Behler, Parrinello and Csányi as the anchors.
responses.response: The impact on simulation is clear, and I respect it as a long-standing colleague with the same entry year. My reservation is about stability. The field is still moving fast toward universal foundation models, the credit splits across two independent lines (Behler-Parrinello networks and Gaussian approximation potentials), and Parrinello's name appears elsewhere. The prize would honour a method whose most consequential form may not have settled yet. I would ask whether the experimental validation is as decisive as for B053 or B011.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat protein electron tunnelling as distinct from the Marcus-recognised electron transfer theory.
How to weigh the experimental programme against the pathway theory of Beratan and Onuchic, which is not credited on this ballot.
Whether Kosugi's earlier tin-amide amination limits the originality credited to Buchwald and Hartwig in B011.
Whether a three-name nitrogenase prize (B003) can be cut without leaving out Dean or Ribbe, and whether the unresolved N2 binding mechanism is acceptable.
The expert reports must show whether B053 has enough support beyond my own ranking to be viable.
statement.conflict_note: My research on cytochrome c oxidase electron and proton transfer is close to B053, and I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou. No personal or institutional tie to Gray or Winkler is apparent from my profile, so I see no required recusal, but the committee should know my field proximity to B053.
